records.title: LexGLUE: A Benchmark Dataset for Legal Language Understanding in English
records.reason: Legal NLU benchmark paper; it contributes datasets and model evaluation for legal-language understanding, not LLM inference systems, serving, memory hierarchy, kernels, quantization, or MoE inference.
records.body_check: Primary ACL Anthology paper page/PDF metadata and paper content describe seven legal NLU datasets and evaluation of generic/legal-oriented language models. The method/evaluation target is legal-domain understanding quality, with no inference-runtime optimization or serving-system mechanism.

records.title: TPP: Transparent Page Placement for CXL-Enabled Tiered-Memory
records.reason: General-purpose CXL tiered-memory page-placement system. It is relevant background for heterogeneous memory, but the paper itself is not an LLM inference/serving system and does not optimize an LLM workload.
records.body_check: Paper metadata and available full-paper descriptions show transparent OS page placement across local and CXL-attached memory, evaluated as a general tiered-memory mechanism. No LLM-specific KV cache, model-weight offload, decoding, or serving pipeline is the target workload.

records.title: The Power of Two Choices in Randomized Load Balancing
records.reason: Foundational randomized load-balancing theory (supermarket model), not an LLM inference or serving paper.
records.body_check: The paper analyzes Poisson arrivals to n servers, d random server choices, FIFO service, equilibrium delay, and asymptotic deterministic approximations. Its system model predates LLMs and contains no LLM serving, GPU scheduling, KV cache, or model inference mechanism.

records.title: Diffusion LLMs Can Do Faster-Than-AR Inference via Discrete Diffusion Forcing
records.reason: Direct LLM inference-acceleration work: D2F combines block-wise autoregressive generation for KV-cache reuse with inter-block parallel diffusion decoding and a pipelined decoder.
records.body_check: Primary arXiv paper describes discrete diffusion forcing, asymmetric distillation, KV-cache-enabled blockwise generation, inter-block parallel decoding, and a pipelined parallel decoding algorithm. Evaluation reports >2.5x inference speed over LLaMA3/Qwen2.5 on GSM8K and >50x over vanilla dLLMs while maintaining comparable quality.

records.title: MMInference: Accelerating Pre-filling for Long-Context VLMs via Modality-Aware Permutation Sparse Attention
records.reason: Inference-system optimization for long-context vision-language models: modality-aware sparse attention plus optimized GPU kernels directly accelerates prefill without retraining.
records.body_check: Primary arXiv paper analyzes modality-specific sparsity including a video Grid pattern, searches per-head sparse patterns offline, constructs sparse distributions dynamically, and supplies optimized GPU kernels. It evaluates LongVila, LLaVA-Video, VideoChat-Flash and Qwen2.5-VL, reporting up to 8.3x prefill acceleration at 1M tokens while maintaining accuracy.

records.title: ThunderKittens: Simple, Fast, and Adorable AI Kernels
records.reason: GPU-kernel framework directly covering attention inference and other model operators; fits the inference-kernel/runtime-compilation lineage despite being broader than LLM-only workloads.
records.body_check: Primary arXiv paper defines warp-level 16x16 tile abstractions, thread-block templates for overlapping asynchronous operations, and grid-level launch/memory hiding. Its evaluated kernels match cuBLAS/FlashAttention-3 on GEMM and attention inference and report 10-40% gains on attention backward, 8x on state-space models, and 14x on linear attention.

records.title: LongGenBench: Long-context Generation Benchmark
records.reason: Benchmark/evaluation work for long-output generation quality, not an inference optimization or serving-system technique.
records.body_check: Primary paper constructs LongGenBench by concatenating questions from MMLU, GSM8K and CommonSenseQA and measuring degradation during long-form generation. Experiments diagnose generation-quality decay (1.2%-47.1%) across models; they do not propose a runtime, memory, scheduling, kernel, cache, quantization, or serving optimization.

records.title: InfiniPot: Infinite Context Processing on Memory-Constrained LLMs
records.reason: Direct KV-cache/memory-constrained inference technique enabling arbitrarily long contexts under a fixed memory budget without additional training.
records.body_check: Primary paper presents Continual Context Distillation, repeatedly compressing a fixed-capacity KV memory 'pot' and selecting retained context with Novelty under Compression and Catalyst Prompt signals. Evaluation targets long-context NLP under constrained memory and compares against long-context/KV compression baselines, making the final application inference memory management.

records.title: Slice-Level Scheduling for High Throughput and Load Balanced LLM Serving
records.reason: Direct LLM-serving scheduling work addressing unpredictable generation lengths, OOM constraints, throughput, and multi-instance load balance.
records.body_check: Primary arXiv paper contrasts sequence-level and iteration-level scheduling, then slices the maximum generation-length budget to bound batch service time/memory and combines this with batching/offloading algorithms. Evaluation reports throughput improvement up to 315.8% and reduced load imbalance versus SLS/ILS schedulers.

records.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
records.reason: Model training/agent capability paper teaching an LM to invoke external APIs; it does not optimize the inference runtime, serving stack, memory hierarchy, kernels, cache, or scheduling.
records.body_check: Full-paper records describe self-supervised construction/filtering of API-call annotations for calculator, QA, search, translation and calendar tools, followed by language-model training and downstream zero-shot evaluation. The contribution is tool-use learning/capability rather than inference-system efficiency.
